question: What explains checkout latency in this window, using only the returned synthetic telemetry?

timeline_observations.statement: Baseline period: request duration ~0.21-0.22 s, request rate 40 rps, connection wait ~1-2 ms, pool utilization 0.6-0.7 under version label v1.

Degraded period starting at the 10:32 bucket: request duration jumps to ~1.04-1.08 s while connection wait rises to ~0.81-0.84 s and v2 pool utilization saturates at 1.0; request rate drops to 10 rps. Bucket boundaries are not exact onset times.

leading_hypothesis.statement: Checkout latency increased because the database connection pool became saturated: in the degraded window pool utilization is 1.0 under version v2 and mean connection wait (~0.82 s) accounts for most of the ~0.83 s increase in mean request duration, despite request rate falling from 40 to 10 rps.
verification_needed: check-001 (unresolvable): confirm pool queuing causality with additional collection, e.g., traces separating connection acquisition from query execution.
check-002 (unresolvable): collect pool_limit configuration for v1 and v2 to test whether v2 is configured with a lower limit explaining saturation.
Why request rate dropped (fewer arrivals vs. throttling/timeouts upstream) is unknown.
No trace or log evidence was retrieved; per-request breakdown of wait vs query time is unavailable.

check-001: Latency increase is caused by connection pool queuing (high pool utilization and connection wait coincide with the latency jump). (unresolvable: Collection ended (decision_budget); this check could not be resolved within the original limits.)

check-002: The v2 connection pool is configured with a lower pool_limit than v1, explaining why utilization saturates at 1.0 and connections queue despite lower request rate. (unresolvable: Review identified this check after collection/context budget exhaustion.)

supporting_findings.statement: Mean request duration rose from ~0.22 s (10:31 bucket) to ~1.04-1.08 s (10:32-10:34 buckets), an increase of roughly 0.8 s.

Mean connection wait rose from ~0.002 s to ~0.81-0.84 s in the same buckets, nearly matching the request duration increase and indicating time spent acquiring connections rather than executing queries.
Pool utilization under version label v2 is 1.0 (fully occupied) in all degraded buckets, versus 0.6-0.7 under v1 in baseline buckets.
The degradation coincides with a version label change from v1 to v2 in pool utilization metrics, and occurs while request rate fell to 10 rps, so saturation is not explained by higher traffic.

contradicting_findings.statement: Request rate dropped from 40 to 10 rps during the degraded window, which is atypical for a load-induced saturation pattern; the cause of the rate drop (e.g., upstream throttling or reduced arrivals) is not observed.
